harness_notes: Each eval seeds a prior session from `files[0]` (passed via --append-system-prompt) and then sends `prompt` (with-skill, plugin loaded) or `baseline_prompt` (no plugin). AskUserQuestion cannot render under `claude -p`, so both configurations are told to treat it as available but print each call's tool input as a fenced json block instead.

evals.baseline_prompt: Before you continue, ask me about anything that's still open.
evals.expected_output: Two rounds are needed. The first AskUserQuestion payload carries the 4 most blocking genuine questions (e.g. export format, overwrite behavior, destination argument vs --output, timestamps), each with a recommended option listed first and per-option reasoning; the user is told a second round follows (gzip, --quiet, tests). The Python-version question (answered by pyproject.toml) and Windows support (answered by the user) are not asked.
expectations: Emits exactly one AskUserQuestion payload (a {questions:[...]} object) for this round
The round contains at most 4 questions
Every question header is 12 characters or fewer
Every question has 2-4 options, with the first (and only the first) labelled '(Recommended)'
No manually added 'Other' option
Every option has a description carrying its reasoning
Does not ask about the Python version (pyproject.toml answers it)
Does not ask about Windows support (the user already answered it)
Tells the user more remains (a further round) or states the assumptions it made instead of asking

The test-runner (vitest) and Redis-client (ioredis) questions are dropped because package.json answers them; req.ip vs socket address is resolved from config.trustProxy rather than asked, or asked with req.ip recommended.
